told.answer: 無, with advice to watch the word day and night
told.t: 若是箇丈夫漢。看箇公案。僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無。州云無。但去二六時中看箇無字。晝參夜參行住坐臥。著衣吃飯處。阿屎放尿處。心心相顧。猛著精彩。守箇無字。日久月深打成一片。忽然心花頓發。悟佛祖之機。
上堂，舉：「僧問趙州：『狗子還有佛性也無？』州云：『無。』僧云：『一切眾生皆有佛性，狗子為什麼却無？』州云：『為伊有業識在。』」師云：「大眾！爾諸人尋常作麼生會？老僧尋常只舉無字便休。爾若透得這一箇字，天下人不柰爾何。爾諸人作麼生透？還有透得徹底麼？有則出來道看。我也不要爾道有，也不要爾道無，也不要爾道不有不無。爾作麼生道？珍重。」
只如僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：有。僧云：既有，為什麼撞入這皮袋？州云：為伊知而故犯。又僧問：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。僧云：一切眾生皆有佛性，狗子為什麼無？州云：為伊有業識在。
復舉僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無。州云有。僧云。為甚撞入者箇皮袋。州云。為他知而故犯。又僧問。狗子還有佛性也無。州云無。僧云。一切眾生皆有佛性。為甚狗子却無州云。為他有業識在。

told.answer: the question twenty times, answered 無
told.t: 僧問趙州：『狗子還有佛性也無？』州云：『無。』爾措大家，多愛穿鑿說道，這箇不是有無之無，乃是真無之無，不屬世間虛豁之無。恁麼說時，還敵得他生死也無？既敵他生死不得，則未是在。既然未是，須是行也提撕，坐也提撕，喜怒哀樂時、應用酬酢時，總是提撕時節。

gloss.若是箇丈夫漢。看箇公案。僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無。州云無。但去二六時中看箇無字: If you are a real man, take up a case. A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.” Just look at the word *mu* all day long. Work on it day and night, walking, standing, sitting and lying down, while you dress and eat, while you shit and piss. Keep your mind on it, moment after moment, with all your strength. Hold on to the word *mu*. As the days and months go by it becomes one piece, and suddenly the flower of the mind opens and you see what the buddhas and patriarchs saw.
gloss.上堂，舉：「僧問趙州：『狗子還有佛性也無？』州云：『無。』僧云：『一切眾生皆有佛: In the hall he raised this: “A monk asked Zhaozhou, ‘Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?’ Zhaozhou said, ‘Mu.’ The monk said, ‘All living beings have Buddha nature. Why doesn’t a dog?’ Zhaozhou said, ‘Because it has karmic consciousness.’” The master said, “Everyone! How do you usually take this? This old monk usually raises the word *mu* and stops there. If you can get through this one word, no one under heaven can do a thing to you. How will you get through it? Has anyone got all the way through? If so, come out and say it. I don’t want you to say it has, I don’t want you to say it doesn’t, and I don’t want you to say it neither has nor hasn’t. What do you say? Take care.”
gloss.只如僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：有。僧云：既有，為什麼撞入這皮袋？州云：為: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Yes.” The monk said, “If it has, why did it push its way into that skin bag?” Zhaozhou said, “Because it knew, and did it anyway.” Another monk asked, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.” The monk said, “All living beings have Buddha nature. Why doesn’t a dog?” Zhaozhou said, “Because it has karmic consciousness.”
gloss.復舉僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無。州云有。僧云。為甚撞入者箇皮袋。州云。為他知而故: He raised this too: a monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Yes.” The monk said, “Then why did it push its way into this skin bag?” Zhaozhou said, “Because it knew, and did it anyway.” Another monk asked, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.” The monk said, “All living beings have Buddha nature. Why doesn’t a dog?” Zhaozhou said, “Because it has karmic consciousness.”
gloss.僧問趙州：『狗子還有佛性也無？』州云：『無。』爾措大家，多愛穿鑿說道，這箇不是有: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.” You scholars love to read things into it, and say this is not the Mu of has and has not but the Mu of true nothingness, not the empty Mu of the world. When you talk like that, can it stand up to birth and death? If it can’t, you haven’t got it yet. And since you haven’t, you must hold it up as you walk and hold it up as you sit. In joy, anger, grief and pleasure, while you deal with people and answer them, it is always the time to hold it up.
